learn.hook: Cross two pencils and look closely — you have just made four angles with a secret pattern!
points: Two lines that meet at a point are called intersecting lines. They make 4 angles at that point.
Angles opposite each other across the meeting point are vertically opposite angles. They are always equal.
Two angles next to each other on a straight line form a linear pair. They add up to 180°.
All four angles around the meeting point add up to 360°.
If one of the four angles is 90°, all four are 90°, and the lines are perpendicular.

example.q: Two lines intersect. One of the angles is 65°. Find the other three angles.
steps: The angle next to 65° on the straight line is 180° − 65° = 115°
The angle opposite 65° is also 65° (vertically opposite)

learn.reallife: Scissor blades, a road crossing and the letter X all show intersecting lines and vertically opposite angles.

quiz.q: Two lines cross. One angle is 65°. What is the angle vertically opposite to it?
quiz.explain: Vertically opposite angles are always equal, so it is 65°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the opposite angle and the given angle add up to 180°

quiz.q: Two lines cross. One angle is 65°. What is the angle next to it on the same straight line?
quiz.explain: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 65° = 115°.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 90° instead of 180°

quiz.q: Two lines intersect and one of the angles is 90°. What are the other three angles?
quiz.explain: The neighbour is 180° − 90° = 90°, and opposite angles are equal. So all four are right angles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only one angle can be a right angle

quiz.q: Two angles form a linear pair and are equal to each other. What is each angle?
quiz.explain: A linear pair adds up to 180°. Two equal parts: 180° ÷ 2 = 90°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each angle of a linear pair is 180°

quiz.q: Three of the four angles where two lines cross are 110°, 70° and 110°. What is the fourth angle?
quiz.explain: All four add to 360°. 360° − (110° + 70° + 110°) = 360° − 290° = 70°. It is also opposite the other 70°.
quiz.mistake: Adds the three angles and forgets to subtract from 360°

quiz.q: Which pair of angles could form a linear pair?
quiz.explain: A linear pair must add up to 180°. Only 100° + 80° = 180°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a linear pair adds up to 90° or that the angles must be equal

quiz.q: Lines AB and CD intersect at O. ∠AOC = 40°. What is ∠AOD?
quiz.explain: ∠AOC and ∠AOD sit side by side on the straight line CD, so they add to 180°. 180° − 40° = 140°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks ∠AOD is vertically opposite to ∠AOC

quiz.q: Which of these is the best example of perpendicular lines?
options: Two edges at the corner of a notebook
The two strokes of the letter V
quiz.explain: The corner of a notebook is a right angle (90°), so its edges are perpendicular.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any two meeting lines are perpendicular

teach.ask: Gappu crossed two sticks and saw four angles. How are these angles connected? Explain!
teach.praise: Wow! Opposite angles are twins and neighbours make 180°. Gappu is amazed!
teach.nudge: What do two neighbouring angles on a straight line add up to?

learn.hook: Railway tracks run side by side for hundreds of kilometres and never bump into each other. How?
points: Parallel lines are lines on a flat surface that never meet, however far you extend them. We write l ∥ m.
Parallel lines stay the same distance apart everywhere.
Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle (90°). We write l ⊥ m.
On a flat page, two different lines either meet (intersect) or are parallel.
If two lines are both perpendicular to the same line, they are parallel to each other.

example.q: Look at the capital letter H. Which parts are parallel and which are perpendicular?
steps: The two upright strokes go the same way and never meet, so they are parallel
The middle bar meets each upright stroke at a right angle
example.answer: The two upright strokes are parallel; the middle bar is perpendicular to both of them.

learn.reallife: Ruled lines in your notebook, the steps of a ladder and the opposite edges of a door are all parallel lines.

games.title: Line truths
items: Parallel lines will meet if you extend them far enough.
Parallel lines never meet, however far you extend them.
Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.
That is the meaning of perpendicular: they meet at 90°.
Two different lines on a flat page that never meet are parallel.
On a flat surface, lines that never meet are parallel.
The two strokes of the letter V are parallel.
They meet at the bottom point, so they are not parallel.
On a flat page, two lines that are both perpendicular to the same line are parallel to each other.
Both make 90° with the same line, so they go the same way.
Every pair of intersecting lines is perpendicular.
Lines can cross at any angle, like 30° or 120°. Only 90° makes them perpendicular.

quiz.q: Which symbol means 'is parallel to'?
quiz.explain: ∥ (two upright strokes side by side) means parallel. ⊥ means perpendicular.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the parallel and perpendicular symbols

quiz.q: Two lines are perpendicular. What is the angle between them?
quiz.explain: Perpendicular lines always meet at a right angle, which is 90°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks perpendicular means a straight line (180°)

quiz.q: Which lines never meet, however far they are extended?
quiz.explain: Parallel lines keep the same distance apart, so they never meet.
quiz.mistake: Thinks perpendicular lines never meet

quiz.q: Riya draws a line l. Then she draws lines m and n, both perpendicular to l. How are m and n related?
options: They are perpendicular to each other
quiz.explain: Both m and n stand at 90° on l, so they point the same way and never meet. They are parallel.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two perpendiculars must cross each other

quiz.q: Which is NOT an example of parallel lines?
quiz.explain: Open scissor blades meet at the screw, so they are intersecting, not parallel.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any two straight edges are parallel

quiz.q: Two parallel lines are 3 cm apart at one place. How far apart are they at another place along the lines?
quiz.explain: Parallel lines are the same distance apart everywhere, so it is still 3 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks parallel lines come closer far away

quiz.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
quiz.explain: Top and bottom sides make one pair, and left and right sides make another pair. That is 2 pairs.
quiz.mistake: Counts each side instead of each pair

quiz.q: How are the two strokes of the capital letter T placed?
quiz.explain: The top bar meets the upright stroke at a right angle, so they are perpendicular.
quiz.mistake: Thinks lines that touch at one end cannot be perpendicular

teach.ask: Gappu is confused: what is the difference between parallel lines and perpendicular lines?
teach.praise: Tweet! Railway tracks are parallel and a notebook corner is perpendicular. Gappu got it!
teach.nudge: Do parallel lines ever meet? And at what angle do perpendicular lines meet?

learn.hook: One road crossing two parallel roads makes 8 angles — and many of them are hidden twins!
points: A transversal is a line that cuts two (or more) lines at different points. With two lines it makes 8 angles.
Corresponding angles are in the same position at each crossing (think of the letter F).
Alternate interior angles lie between the two lines on opposite sides of the transversal (think of the letter Z).
If the two lines are parallel: corresponding angles are equal, alternate interior angles are equal, and interior angles on the same side add up to 180°.
If corresponding angles (or alternate angles) are equal, then the two lines are parallel.

example.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 70°. Find its corresponding angle, its alternate interior angle and the interior angle on the same side.
steps: Interior angles on the same side add up to 180°: 180° − 70° = 110°

learn.reallife: Zebra crossings, window grills and the lines of a badminton court show transversals cutting parallel lines.

quiz.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 70°. What is its corresponding angle?
quiz.explain: When lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal. So it is 70°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks corresponding angles add up to 180°

quiz.q: Lines p and q are parallel. ∠3 = 125° and ∠5 is its alternate interior angle. What is ∠5?
quiz.explain: Alternate interior angles between parallel lines are equal, so ∠5 = 125°.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 180° as if it were a linear pair

quiz.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One interior angle is 75°. What is the interior angle on the same side?
quiz.explain: Interior angles on the same side add up to 180°. 180° − 75° = 105°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks these angles are equal like alternate angles

quiz.q: A transversal cuts two lines, and a pair of corresponding angles are both 60°. What can you say about the two lines?
quiz.explain: Equal corresponding angles tell us the two lines are parallel.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that equal corresponding angles prove the lines are parallel

quiz.q: A transversal cuts two lines. A pair of corresponding angles are 80° and 85°. What can you say?
options: The transversal is parallel to them
quiz.explain: If the lines were parallel, the corresponding angles would be equal. 80° ≠ 85°, so the lines are not parallel.
quiz.mistake: Thinks angles that are close are good enough

quiz.q: A transversal cuts two lines at two different points. How many angles are formed in all?
quiz.explain: Each crossing point makes 4 angles. Two crossing points make 4 + 4 = 8 angles.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the angles at one crossing

quiz.q: A transversal is perpendicular to one of two parallel lines. One interior angle is 90°. What is the interior angle on the same side?
quiz.explain: Same-side interior angles add up to 180°. 180° − 90° = 90°, so the transversal is perpendicular to both lines.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the other angle must be 180°

quiz.q: In the letter Z, the top and bottom strokes are parallel. The angle at the top corner is 40°. What is the angle at the bottom corner?
quiz.explain: The two corner angles of a Z are alternate interior angles between parallel strokes, so they are equal: 40°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the two angles add up to 180°

teach.ask: Gappu sees a road crossing two parallel railway tracks. Which angles are equal, and which add up to 180°?
teach.praise: Fantastic! F and Z angles are twins, and C angles make 180°. Gappu salutes you!
teach.nudge: Which angle pairs are equal when the lines are parallel?
